newsitem.title: UK: U.S. data gives shot in arm to Euro markets.
newsitem.headline: U.S. data gives shot in arm to Euro markets.

text.p: European stock markets rallied strongly on Tuesday after lower-than-expected U.S. prices data eased the pressure on American policy-makers to raise interest rates again.
The 0.1 percent rise in the March consumer price index (CPI) was half market expectations, sparking a a sharp rise in U.S. stocks and bonds.
The dollar rose to a fresh 37-month high against the mark, while sterling stormed to a 55-month peak against the German currency.
European bourses, already showing moderate gains, accelerated as Wall Street opened with a bang and the Dow Industrials Average had put on around 80 points by the time Europe closed.
"The markets had factored in a lot of bad news and now it's running on relief," said one London equities dealer.

While the March CPI figure was balm to the financial markets, economists warned U.S. policymakers would need to see a slowing in consumer demand or overall economic growth before backing away from their current monetary tightening.
"These (CPI) figures clearly show that inflation remains subdued, but it won't stop the Fed from tightening," said DKB International economist Nick Stamenkovic.

The market reaction displayed by the major European bourses was reflected amongst second-tier markets, too. Amsterdam's AEX index closed with gains of 2.8 percent, GMT, while Milan's MIBTEL ended up 2.08 percent and Madrid's IBEX 35 2.4 percent.
Among the majors, the French and German bourses bounded ahead the best.

Frankfurt climbed more than two percent in post-bourse electronic trading after traders saw the Dow's early spurt. The 30-share DAX earlier ended floor trade before the CPI figures were released with a gain of 47.78 points, or 1.46 percent, to 3,327.68.

"The U.S. consumer prices data was encouraging but nobody should go mega-bullish on it. It was a relief to the nervousness which has been around since last Friday and there is support coming from the firm dollar and stronger Bunds," one share trader warned, however.

Carmaker Volkswagen was yanked both ways over the day after a report showing a three percent drop in European new car registrations during March. Volkswagen shares ended at 1,056.50 marks, up 6.70 marks, in late IBIS trade.
French shares also closed 2.12 percent higher, the CAC-40 ending up 54.50 points at 2,620.63. Volume was 6.2 billion francs.
Software group Cap Gemini was the top gainer of the day, adding 8.66 percent to 364 francs.

Luxury goods group LVMH was boosted by a big rise in 1997 first quarter results and added 4.66 percent to 1,347 francs. Christian Dior , which has a big stake in LVMH, posted a four percent gain to 846 francs.
The London stock exchange, Europe's biggest bourse, joined the party but failed to achieve the gains seen elsewhere. The blue chip FTSE 100 index closed 35.1 points, or 0.83 percent, at 4,286.8.
Some strategists doubted whether the rebound would last.

"This is a bit of a holiday in the sun for the markets, but I don't think this is a sign that the Fed is not going to tighten further," said stock strategist David Aserkoff of Credit Suisse First Boston.
"The market was geared up for a bigger rise. We don't think this rise is sustainable."
On the foreign exchange market, the dollar pushed its way to a fresh 37-month high of 1.7375 marks with the help of strong U.S. asset markets following the CPI data.
The British pound also hit a 55-month peak at 2.8231 marks, boosted by strong demand from U.S. investors enticed by the unit's attractive yield.
With the market having mostly priced in another rise in key U.S. rates in the near future, its attention for the moment was on the performance of U.S. stocks and bonds, analysts said.

"While this (speculation of higher U.S. rates) is a bullish factor for the dollar, in the short-term people will be looking at the assets markets' response," said Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange analyst at Merrill Lynch in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7333 marks and 126.28 yen after ending at 1.7228 marks and 126.45 yen in late trading in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS --CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 35.1 points, or 0.83 percent, at 4,286.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 54.5 points, or 2.12 percent, at 2,620.63.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade up 47.78 points, or 1.46 percent, at 3,327.68. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX ended was up 71.74 points, or 2.18 percent, at 3,369.26.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended at $341.75, down $4.80, while silver was down three cents at $4.70.
